question: Should an over-buffered session subscriber be disconnected during reset/delete/replacement, or should `socket.drain` remain best-effort and preserve the connection?
rationale: The patch currently selects forced disconnect through an implicit broadcaster default, trading lifecycle signaling against client availability without an established public Gateway contract.

options.title: Preserve connections
options.body: Send drains with normal slow-client shedding, document them as advisory, and require clients to reconcile after sequence gaps or reconnects.

options.title: Approve bounded disconnect
options.body: Keep close-on-slow semantics only with an explicit recovery contract, documentation, saturated-socket tests, and real reconnect proof.

recommendation.title: Preserve connections
recommendation.body: Send drains with normal slow-client shedding, document them as advisory, and require clients to reconcile after sequence gaps or reconnects.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history most directly connects this person to the Gateway broadcaster and session-change implementation where the contract is enforced.
